summary: Honoré-Joseph Chavée worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at KU Leuven under Félix Nève and later under Eugène Burnouf. He taught at the Collège Stanislas de Paris, served as professor at Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa, and taught at the École Supérieure de Guerre.

A scholar in Buddhist studies, Honsho Ueda served as a lecturer (attested 1963) and professor (attested 1992) at Minobusan Junior College, professor at Minobusan University (attested 1996), and director at the Institute for Advanced Studies on Asia (attested 1996).
Working in Sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, Hoong Teik Toh earned a PhD from Harvard University by 2004, where he studied under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, and Yudru Tsomu.

Horace Arthur Rose specialized in Indology and history and archaeology. He was educated at St Paul's School and Emmanuel College (~1886–1889) and served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service from 1888 to 1917.

Wales worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After studying at Queens' College and earning a PhD under Charles Otto Blagden at SOAS, he served as Field Director for the Greater India Society (~1934–1941) and Vice-president of the Royal Asiatic Society (1964–1968).

An Indologist who studied medicine at St Thomas's Hospital and Sanskrit under Henry Thomas Colebrooke, Wilson served as Boden Professor of Sanscrit at the University of Oxford (1831–1860) and Director of the Royal Asiatic Society (1837–1860).

Indologist Horace Irvin Poleman studied at the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown. He held posts at Pennsylvania, Yale, and the US Embassy in New Delhi, and headed the South Asia Section (1938–1949) and Oriental Division (1955–1965) at the Library of Congress.

Horace L. Friess worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Columbia University (~1915–1918) and Heidelberg University (~1924–1925), joining Columbia's faculty in 1919 and serving as Joseph L. Buttenwieser Professor of Human Relations from 1962 to 1966.
Working in Tibetology, Horkhang Sonam Palbar studied under Tsadru Ngawang Losang as well as Gendun Chophel between approximately 1946 and 1951.
Horst Brinkhaus is an Indologist who held an attested post at the University of Münster in 1978 and subsequently served at Kiel University from around 1995 to 2008.
Horst Fichtner, who worked in Indology and history and archaeology, completed his Dr. med. at the University of Leipzig by 1924 and taught social ethics at Humboldt University of Berlin in 1945.

Horst Lasic, a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, was a researcher at the Austrian Academy of Sciences (1995). He earned his PhD at the University of Vienna by 1999 and became a lecturer in Tibetan and Sanskrit there in 1999.

A scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, Hosakote Krishna Sastri served in the Archaeological Survey of India as Assistant Superintendent for Epigraphy (~1904–1925) and as Government Epigraphist for India (~1920–1925).

Working in philosophy and religious studies, Hoseok Leigh earned a PhD from the California Institute of Integral Studies (attested 2010), having studied under Ha-u Kim and the traditional teacher Cheonghwa.
Hoseong Kim is a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Attested in 2011, he served as a professor at Dongguk University and founded the Nihon Bukkyōshi Kenkyūjo.
Hoshu Mitsuhara worked in Buddhist studies. He held academic positions at Koyasan University, serving as a professor (attested 1982) and later as professor emeritus (attested 2004).

Hotetsu Matsumoto works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He held a post at Tohoku University (attested 1997) and serves as professor and director of the Clinical Esoteric Buddhism Center at Shuchiin University (attested 2026).

Hoyo Watanabe was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Rissho University (~1952–1961). He remained there throughout his career, serving as professor (~1974–2004), Dean of Buddhist Studies (attested 1984–1985), and special honorary professor (~2004–2021).
Hozen Seki was a figure in Buddhist studies who founded the American Buddhist Academy and served as resident minister at the New York Buddhist Church (attested 1998).

Adjarian worked in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Heinrich Hübschmann at Strasbourg, with Antoine Meillet as mentor. He held posts at Aramiyan School, Sanasarian College, and Yerevan State University (1923).
